title: Who is better at math, Jenny or Jingzhen? Uncovering Stereotypes in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: Stereotypical association of religious identities with specific gender-by-ethnicity groups. This was measured through perplexity scores (APX) on sentence templates and through analysis of generated character profiles.
findings: LLMs demonstrate strong, consistent stereotypical associations between ethnicities and religions (e.g., Arabs/Muslims, Indians/Hindus, Israelis/Jews, Japanese/Shinto). Religion was found to be the most influential feature for distinguishing between ethnicities in generated character profiles. These biases were consistent across the models' internal representations (measured by APX) and their generative outputs, reinforcing harmful stereotypes like the association of Muslims with terrorism.
